editions.title: Joshua Kushner Wants To Buy FIFA For $4.2B

stories.headline: FIFA Plans To Sell Commercial Rights Stake For $4.2B To Private Investors
body: The global soccer body is offering a 21% stake to an investor group led by venture capitalist Joshua Kushner.
This deal would raise $4.2B to triple development funding for member nations, giving smaller countries vital cash to grow the sport.
European soccer authority UEFA strongly opposes the sale, arguing that the sport belongs to fans and should never be sold for private profit.

stories.headline: LIV Golf Cancels $40M Michigan Team Championship Amid Funding Doubts
body: The Saudi-backed golf league is scrapping its August season finale, eliminating a planned $40M prize pool for the participating teams.
The cancellation occurs as the Saudi Public Investment Fund, the league's primary financial backer, plans to halt its support after this season.
With two tournaments left in a shortened schedule, the organization is urgently seeking $350M from new investors to survive into 2027.

stories.headline: Sports Prediction Exchange ProphetX Raises $35M To Expand Platform
body: The federally regulated sports exchange secured the funds from investment firms Parlay Capital and Data Point Capital to scale its platform.
Active users and platform assets grew by 50% in 30 days after the company received federal approval to operate.
Unlike traditional sportsbooks, the platform lets users trade directly with each other and aims to triple its trading volume by 2026.

stories.headline: Notre Dame Signs $20M Jersey Patch Deal With SoFi
body: The university will place logos from financial services company SoFi on its uniforms in an agreement worth up to $20M annually.
The new revenue will help offset soaring athletic expenses, as assembling a modern college football roster now costs over $40M.

stories.headline: Ohio State Signs $17M Jersey Patch Deal With JPMorganChase
body: Banking giant JPMorganChase will pay $17M annually to put its logo on uniforms for all 36 sports teams at Ohio State University.
This college sponsorship exceeds the average $10M per season earned by professional NBA teams for similar jersey advertising.

stories.headline: Major League Soccer Proposes Flexible Salary Cap To Boost Team Spending
body: The US soccer league will review a plan to remove complex spending limits, allowing teams to freely invest across their entire rosters.
Sparked by the arrival of global star Lionel Messi, the rule overhaul aims to elevate overall team quality ahead of the 2027 season.
Improving team quality is critical to boosting television ratings before the league's current $275M annual broadcasting contract with tech giant Apple expires in 2029.

stories.headline: 2026 WNBA All-Star Game Sets Attendance Record And Surpasses NBA Counterpart
body: The Chicago event hosted nearly 20K fans, breaking league records and outdrawing the men's NBA All-Star Game for the first time ever.
League Commissioner Cathy Engelbert announced a record 73M viewers by mid-season, easily beating the previous full-season record of 63M.
This massive growth follows expanded national TV coverage and a historic union contract that secured major salary increases for players.

stories.headline: Germany Plans Bid To Host The Men's World Cup In 2038 Or 2042
body: German football executive Axel Hellmann confirmed the national sports association is preparing a World Cup hosting campaign utilizing the country's strong existing infrastructure.
The event requires significant public investment to modernize stadiums, aiming to replicate the massive global branding boost of their 2006 tournament.
Hellmann also criticized global soccer governing body FIFA for record-high match tickets, warning that expensive admission creates social barriers excluding everyday fans.

stories.headline: Activists Demand Public Vote on $600M City Funding for New Royals Stadium
body: The baseball franchise and greeting card maker Hallmark plan to build a $3B downtown stadium and entertainment district by 2031.
Labor advocacy groups are demanding a citizen vote on an already approved $600M city funding package for the project.
This public pressure follows an April 2024 vote where local residents strongly rejected using taxpayer money for a new ballpark.

stories.headline: Real Madrid Becomes First Football Club To Surpass €1.2B In Revenue
body: The Spanish sports giant reached €1.2B in sales, driven heavily by €363M from its newly renovated stadium and strong marketing.
Despite these massive earnings, the team holds just €83M in cash and relies on credit lines to cover expensive player salaries.
The organization reported a modest €26M profit and plans to use its financial power to spend over €100M on new star players.

stories.headline: Spanish Women’s Soccer League Accepts $64.5M Investment From Pau Gasol's Firm
body: Spain's Liga F accepted $64.5M from an investment group led by former NBA star Pau Gasol to fund immediate league growth.
In exchange for the cash, the league will share nearly half of its broadcast and sponsorship revenue with the investors for 25 years.
Major soccer club Real Madrid rejected the deal, arguing that trading decades of future profits for a quick cash payout hurts long-term sustainability.

stories.headline: DAZN Investor Aser Ventures Explores Selling Part Of Its Stake In The Sports Streamer
body: Aser Ventures, the investment firm of former Leeds United owner Andrea Radrizzani, wants cash to fund its own sports and technology bets.
Aser gained roughly 5% of DAZN, worth about $400M, when the streamer bought its Eleven Group in 2023; later fundraising diluted that holding.
DAZN, backed by billionaire Len Blavatnik, lost $936M in 2024, down from $1.4B, and is restructuring to raise money or list publicly.

stories.headline: Pasadena's Rose Bowl Secures $80M To Modernize Ahead Of 2028 Olympics
body: Venue CEO Jens Weiden launched an $80M campaign using private donations and local taxes so the stadium avoids relying on public city funds.
The upcoming Los Angeles 2028 Olympics will fund permanent infrastructure upgrades, while renovations add wider seats and a premium club for 1K guests.
This careful strategy preserves the historic landmark without demolition, ensuring it remains a profitable sports venue and vital emergency base for regional crises.

stories.headline: NFL Flag Championships Reach Record 14.3M Viewers On Disney Networks
body: The youth flag football tournament attracted 14.3M unique viewers on major Disney-owned TV channels like ABC and ESPN.
The girls' high school championship game set an all-time record with 1.12M viewers, highlighting the sport's rapid growth.
Overall event viewership spiked 50% compared to last year, fueled by the organization's enormous base of 830K youth athletes.

stories.headline: Zuffa Boxing Pivots To Co-Promoted Events While Awaiting Federal Legislation
body: Boxing promotion Zuffa, backed by UFC parent TKO, is abandoning its solo-league model to co-promote title fights with established boxing organizations.
Zuffa fighter Conor Benn will co-headline a non-Zuffa match that sold $6.3M in initial tickets, showing the financial power of cross-promoted events.
The company must delay its standalone league plans until the Senate passes pending federal legislation designed to restructure the business rules of boxing.

stories.headline: Irish Laya Arena Unveils €52M Redevelopment For Dublin Horse Show
body: The €52M joint venture by event venue RDS and professional rugby team Leinster upgraded the stadium to hold over 20K spectators.
Healthcare brand Laya Healthcare secured naming rights and debuts a premium fan experience at next week's Dublin Horse Show.
This significant commercial investment improves spectator hospitality and provides a modern platform for future Irish sporting and entertainment events.

stories.headline: College Sports Commission Approves $7.5M Payment Deal For Nebraska Football
body: Eighteen Nebraska football players will share a $7.5M payment funded by Playfly, the university's multimedia marketing partner.
An oversight board initially rejected the contracts because the athletes were being paid without being required to perform any specific promotional duties.
Nebraska successfully restructured the contracts, creating a blueprint for other schools to bypass the strict $20.5M limit on direct player payments.

stories.headline: Judge Advances Patent Lawsuit Against NFL Over Mobile App Video Casting
body: Err Content IP, a technology patent owner, sued the football league for allegedly copying its method of casting videos from smartphones to televisions.
The NFL claims its app does not infringe because the video casting actually relies on native smartphone software, like Samsung features.
The judge ruled the lawsuit can proceed to discovery, forcing both sides to share private internal emails and potential trade secrets.

stories.headline: London-Based Financial Firm IG Group Acquires Betting App Underdog For Up To $1.3B
body: London-based financial firm IG Group will pay at least $1.1B, plus up to $850M in employee bonuses for hitting high earnings goals.
The deal gives IG Group entry into the prediction market space, which allows nationwide betting by bypassing individual state gambling laws.
The rapidly growing app recently became profitable, producing $59.6M in earnings while reaching over 950K monthly active users.

stories.headline: Jake Paul's MVP Merges With PFL To Form New MMA Company
body: The new mixed martial arts business will operate under the brand of MVP, a sports promotion firm led by influencer Jake Paul.
This merger combines MVP with PFL, an established fighting league, to create a larger platform intended to challenge the dominant UFC.
Founders aim to disrupt the industry's traditional business model by offering athletes fairer pay and a modernized stage to become global stars.

stories.headline: Soccer Federations Reject FIFA's $4.2B World Cup Sale Plan And Question President Gianni Infantino
body: World soccer governing body FIFA proposed selling a 21% stake in its events to private investors to raise $4.2B for its member groups.
European soccer group UEFA and North American group Concacaf rejected the idea, with UEFA threatening a total boycott if it proceeds.
The massive backlash has caused member groups to lose confidence in FIFA President Gianni Infantino ahead of his upcoming re-election bid.

stories.headline: NWSL Cancels Broadcast Deal With Streaming Platform Victory+ Over Unpaid Fees
body: The National Women's Soccer League terminated its contract with streaming service Victory+ because the platform failed to make its required payments.
The 57 affected matches will now stream on the league's own free app, maintaining accessibility within its broader $240M media strategy.
The financially struggling streaming service recently lost similar partnerships with major baseball and hockey teams after failing to secure new funding.

stories.headline: Minnesota Timberwolves Sign Five-Year Exclusive Streaming Deal With DAZN
body: The NBA team will move its local games to DAZN, a global sports streaming platform, after its previous broadcast partner collapsed.
Fans must use the app to watch matchups since they will no longer be available on traditional cable or satellite television.
While exact monthly subscription costs remain unannounced, the franchise will offer 15 local games for free to ease the transition.

stories.headline: Major League Soccer Owners Vote To Select Next Commissioner
body: Larry Berg, co-owner of a Los Angeles soccer franchise valued over $1B, is the favorite against former Fox media executive David Nathanson.
The winner needs a two-thirds majority vote to replace Don Garber, who has led the growing soccer league since 1999.
To avoid conflicts, the selected candidate must sell their team investments before officially taking over as commissioner after the 2026 season.

stories.headline: NWSL Plans Earliest Season Start In 2027 To Accommodate World Cup
body: The National Women’s Soccer League, America's top female soccer tier, will launch its 2027 season on February 11 to mark its earliest start ever.
This schedule shift creates a two-month summer pause so players can compete in the 2027 Women's World Cup without missing standard league games.
The winter kickoff introduces logistical hurdles for clubs, including freezing weather conditions and scheduling conflicts with shared men's professional soccer stadiums.

stories.headline: NBA Cancels Middle East Preseason Games Over Ongoing US-Iran War
body: The professional basketball league canceled its Abu Dhabi preseason events for the first time in five years due to the ongoing U.S.-Iran war.
Abu Dhabi's tourism department remains a major NBA business partner, hoping to eventually host 22.5K fans at a new regional high-tech arena.
With no timeline for a Middle East return, the league will instead play international exhibition games in Paris, Mexico City, and Manchester.

stories.headline: Former NFL Quarterback Tony Romo Arrested For Intoxicated Driving
body: Police arrested Romo, a prominent CBS television sports analyst, after he failed field sobriety tests on July 23.
Authorities stopped his vehicle for illegally passing highway traffic on the shoulder and discovered an open alcohol bottle inside.
He received three citations carrying over $1.5K in total fines and has a court hearing scheduled for September.

stories.headline: FIFA Abandons $4.2B Stake Sale in Commercial Operations Following Widespread Backlash
body: World football governing body FIFA planned to raise $4.2B by selling a 21% stake in its events business to private investors.
The deal collapsed after major regional football groups threatened tournament boycotts and key internal advisors publicly condemned the controversial proposal.
Scrapping this plan leaves FIFA president Gianni Infantino politically vulnerable to potential challengers ahead of the upcoming 2027 leadership elections.

stories.headline: Tech Billionaire Nikesh Arora Bids Over $1B For New London NBA Europe Team
body: Nikesh Arora, CEO of cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks, is leading an investor group offering over $1B for the proposed London franchise.
The NBA plans to launch a new 16-team European basketball league in late 2027 to expand its global reach.
Over 120 investors, including major sovereign wealth funds, submitted league bids ranging from $500M to more than $1B.

stories.headline: DC Open Tennis Tournament Quadruples Revenue Since 2019
body: Venture capitalist Mark Ein bought the event in 2019 and boosted sales by improving fan experiences, achieving a 100% ticket sellout rate annually.
Despite surging profits, total player payouts only grew 91% because global tour rules detach individual event financial success from the actual prize money.
To support this rapid growth, the local government approved a $10M investment to upgrade the aging public tennis facility for players and fans.

stories.headline: DirecTV Retains Commercial Rights To Distribute NFL Sunday Ticket
body: Satellite provider DirecTV will continue broadcasting out-of-market football games to 300K commercial locations like bars.
EverPass, a media distributor backed by the NFL, originally planned to cut satellite access entirely.
The partnership protects DirecTV's valuable commercial business while incentivizing it to sell EverPass streaming subscriptions.

stories.headline: Major College Sports Conferences Back Senate Bill Regulating Athlete Pay
body: The Big Ten and SEC, two powerful college sports leagues, agreed to support a bipartisan bill protecting the sport's governing body from lawsuits.
The compromise raises the athlete payment limit to over $40M, giving schools more legal ways to fairly compensate top talent.
Lawmakers are rushing to pass the legislation before an August recess to establish clear, nationwide rules for athlete transfers and pay.

stories.headline: Athletes Unlimited Pro Basketball Pauses 2027 Season Amid Rising Competition
body: Athletes Unlimited, a sports network backed by $30M in funding, is halting its basketball league to reevaluate its long-term strategy.
The decision follows a major pay raise in the WNBA, the primary US women's league, which now requires a $270K minimum salary.
Rival winter leagues, such as Unrivaled and Project B, are also capturing top talent by offering lucrative six-figure and multimillion-dollar contracts.

stories.headline: Federal Judge Blocks NCAA From Denying Fifth Year Of Eligibility To College Athletes
body: A judge ordered the NCAA, college sports' governing body, to let a nationwide class of recent graduates play a fifth season for sponsorship money.
The NCAA plans a swift appeal, arguing the rushed decision creates roster chaos and takes valuable scholarships away from incoming freshmen.
Major athletic conferences are backing a US bill granting the NCAA legal immunity to control rosters for athletes generating $1B+ in revenue.

stories.headline: First US Women's Pro Baseball League In 72 Years Sells Out Opening Game
body: The WPBL features four city-based teams and was co-founded by Justine Siegal, the first woman to coach a men's pro baseball team.
The league selected 60 players for its rosters from a pool of over 600 global applicants, showing massive demand for the sport.
All inaugural season games will occur in Springfield, Illinois, with major sports broadcaster ESPN streaming 37 matchups to a national audience.

stories.headline: New York Sues Prediction Market Kalshi for $36B Over Illegal Gambling
body: New York accuses Kalshi, a federally licensed prediction platform, of illegal gambling and demands $36B in damages and $100K penalties per illegal bet.
Kalshi quickly moved the lawsuit to federal court, arguing that state officials cannot shut down an exchange approved by the federal government.
The national regulatory agency overseeing these markets stepped in to protect Kalshi, highlighting a growing nationwide legal battle over online event betting.

stories.headline: LIV Golf Seeks $350M In New Investment As Saudi Backer Prepares To End Funding
body: Professional golf league LIV is hosting a $30M tournament this week but is expected to cancel its $40M season finale in Michigan.
The league is actively seeking $350M from private investors because its primary backer, the Saudi Public Investment Fund, will end support this season.
Canceling the finale saves the league $40M in prize money as it navigates this financial transition to survive without its original funding.

stories.headline: Sportradar Swings To $4M Quarterly Loss Despite Revenue Growth
body: The sports data firm, which sells live match data to betting operators, lost $4.0M, reversing a $56.6M profit a year earlier.
Revenue rose 18.9%, but the cost of buying sports data rights jumped 29.7% to $159M, erasing the gains.
Sportradar pointed to World Cup betting, $2.5B wagered across 353M tickets, and renewed rights deals including Wimbledon.

stories.headline: UFC Parent TKO Reports Strong Revenue Growth Despite A $30M Event Loss
body: Parent company TKO Group Holdings earned $1.5B in total revenue, driven by strong growth from both UFC and professional wrestling brand WWE.
The mixed martial arts league UFC lost $30M hosting a free event at the White House, which temporarily lowered its profit margins.
Despite this unique expense, record merchandise sales and 34M global viewers helped the parent company raise its future earnings projections.

stories.headline: Aston Martin Creditors Threaten Legal Action Over Plan To Sell Brand Rights
body: Creditors owed about $1.75B sent a legal warning, saying they may unwind July's $738M loan led by BlackRock-owned HPS Investment Partners.
The loan reportedly requires transferring 50.1% of Aston Martin's non-car branding rights to Authentic Brands, a US brand owner.
The 113-year-old carmaker is losing money as weak sales, US tariffs and soft Chinese demand drain cash, forcing cost cuts and new borrowing.

stories.headline: Private Equity Executive Larry Berg Chosen As New MLS Commissioner
body: Berg, an executive at private equity firm Apollo Global Management, will sell his stake in the LAFC soccer team to lead the league.
His finance background fits a growing trend, with 16 of the 30 MLS teams now backed by private equity investors.
Berg replaces long-time leader Don Garber, inheriting a league with five teams valued over $1B and a $2.5B Apple media deal.

stories.headline: NCAA Seeks Emergency Block On Court Ruling Granting Older Athletes An Extra Year Of Play
body: A federal judge recently allowed a group of college athletes to play a fifth year so they can earn more endorsement money.
The NCAA, college sports' governing body, argues this extension will force schools to unexpectedly cut younger players from tightly capped team rosters.
The sports association wants an appeals court to pause the ruling before the upcoming fall semester begins and team rosters are permanently locked.

stories.headline: U.S. Soccer Extends Coach Mauricio Pochettino Through 2030 With Billionaire Backing
body: The extension is heavily funded by Ken Griffin, the billionaire founder of investment firm Citadel, continuing his past financial support.
While exact terms are private, continuing his original $6M annual salary would cost an estimated $24M over the four years.
The deal ensures team stability and gives the coach new authority to guide American youth soccer development and coaching education.

stories.headline: Liverpool Plans First U.S. Stores In Push To 40 Shops Worldwide
body: The Premier League club has 26 stores globally and wants 40 by 2030, with America now the target.
The U.S. is Liverpool's biggest retail market outside Britain, making up 26% of international sales and 26M fans.
Merchandise is a key earner as European spending rules cap clubs at what they make, currently $428M commercially.

stories.headline: Global Football Associations Withdraw Re-Election Support For FIFA President
body: FIFA President Gianni Infantino sparked outrage by trying to sell a 21% business stake to Joshua Kushner's private investment fund for $4.2B.
The English Football Association and other national governing bodies are officially revoking their endorsements for his 2027 re-election bid.
Although he cancelled the controversial sale, the severe backlash means Infantino may now face a serious challenger instead of running unopposed.

stories.headline: Former US congressman George Santos Pays $35K To Settle Prediction Market Trading Probe
body: The former lawmaker traded on Kalshi, a regulated prediction platform, placing bets on whether he would personally attend a presidential speech.
US commodities regulators found he posted misleading social media updates to manipulate contract prices, allowing him to illegally pocket over $17.5K.
Santos agreed to forfeit his profits, pay a matching $17.5K civil fine, and accept a three-year ban from the platform.
